# pcd_compute_service (Resource)

Controls whether Nova schedules new instances onto a hypervisor: the PCD UI's Enable/Disable Scheduling and Enable/Disable Maintenance Mode on a host. It manages the host's existing `nova-compute` service record, so creating it changes the service's status rather than creating anything, and destroying it re-enables scheduling. Creating it waits up to ten minutes for the host's `nova-compute` service to register, which happens once its hypervisor role has converged. `status = "maintenance"` only disables scheduling, with the reason the PCD UI writes, so the UI shows the host in maintenance; it moves no instances. To move them off, run the `pcd_compute_host_drain` action afterward (Terraform 1.14 or later). On a cluster with a single hypervisor, disabling it stops new instances and, per the PCD UI, most other VM operations in that cluster until it is enabled again. Requires an admin token.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pcd_host" "hyp1" {
  name = "hyp1.example.com"
}

# Stop new instances from landing on this hypervisor (the PCD UI's Disable
# Scheduling). "maintenance" does the same with the reason the UI writes, so
# the UI shows the host in maintenance; destroying the resource enables
# scheduling again.
resource "pcd_compute_service" "hyp1" {
  host_id = data.pcd_host.hyp1.id
  status  = "disabled"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host_id` (String) The hypervisor's resmgr host UUID: `data.pcd_host.<name>.id` or `pcd_host_cluster_role.<name>.host_id`. PCD names the host's compute service after it. Reference the hypervisor's `pcd_host_cluster_role` so this resource is created after the role and destroyed before it. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `status` (String) `enabled` schedules new instances onto the host. `disabled` stops that and leaves running instances where they are. `maintenance` is `disabled` with the reason the PCD UI writes for maintenance mode (`<uuid>:<epoch milliseconds>`); a host already in maintenance keeps its reason, including one the UI wrote. A host disabled with any other reason (from the CLI, for example) reads as `maintenance` too. The UI offers maintenance only from `enabled`; Nova and this resource also allow it from `disabled`.

### Read-Only

- `compute_state` (String) Whether the host's `nova-compute` is reporting in: `up` or `down`. Informational.
- `disabled_reason` (String) The reason Nova holds for the disabled service; null when it has none.
- `id` (String) The host ID, the same as `host_id`.
- `service_id` (String) The Nova service UUID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax. The IDs are assigned by PCD; the
[Importing guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/platform9/pcd/latest/docs/guides/importing)
explains how to look them up.

```shell
# The import ID is the hypervisor's resmgr host UUID:
#   pcdctl compute service list --service nova-compute -c Host
terraform import pcd_compute_service.hyp1 <host_id>
```
